rejected_findings.issue: The GPU test's mock of subprocess.run swallows the real encode, so the test does not test what it claims (a part opening on a stack2 keeps bt709 and its range through a real render); it only checks the filtergraph string. The class docstring says 'run on GPU0 under the lease: must fail on the old code, pass on the new', but the mocked run never encodes, so the old code would also pass this test (the old code's graph also ends each shot's chain with setsar=1:1, just without the setparams, and the assertion only checks the new code's expected substring).

with mock.patch.object(RV, "_input_colour", lambda p: colour), \

rejected_findings.fix: Split the graph-assertion into the CPU test (where it already lives) and let the GPU test run the real encode, or assert the old code's graph would fail the same assertion (e.g. check the setparams substring is actually new).

rejected_findings.issue: The probe test's second case asserts primaries=bt470bg and colorspace=smpte170m survive, but the third case (all-unknown) returns '' and the first case's expected string orders range first; the dict-iteration order of _KNOWN (Python 3.7+ insertion order) makes the output order deterministic, but the test hard-codes that order, coupling the test to _KNOWN's declaration order rather than to the documented contract ('known values only').
rejected_findings.fix: Parse the returned options into a dict/set before comparing, or sort both sides, so the test checks the contract (known values kept, unknown dropped) rather than the incidental option order.

missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.issue: _input_colour parses ffprobe output by whitespace-splitting lines; a value containing a space or an unexpected extra key would corrupt the dict, and any ffprobe failure (nonzero returncode) is silently treated as no colour, so the part renders untagged with no warning — the very failure mode this fix targets can recur silently.
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.evidence: got = dict(x.split("=", 1) for x in r.stdout.split() if "=" in x); return ":".join(...) with no check of r.returncode
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.fix: Check r.returncode and log/skip gracefully, or use -of json / -of csv=p=0 like the old _input_matrix did, which was immune to key=value line parsing.
